name: Better Stack
summary: Better Stack is an observability platform that catches app errors, records session replays, and checks your site's uptime, all from one dashboard.

free_plan_covers.note: The free plan includes 100,000 exceptions, 5,000 session replays and 10 uptime monitors a month on one account, each with 90-day retention.

first_paid_usd_month.note: There's no single paid plan; past the free limits, each product bills separately, for example $25/month per 50 extra uptime monitors plus a small per-exception and per-replay rate.

portability.note: Error tracking works by pointing the standard @sentry/nextjs SDK at a Better Stack DSN instead of Sentry's, so switching error tools later can mean changing a URL instead of rewriting how errors are captured.

uptime_checks.note: Uptime monitoring checks a URL from outside on a schedule and alerts you when it's down; the free plan includes 10 monitors and heartbeats.

session_replay.note: Session Replay records what a person did before an error; the free plan includes 5,000 replays a month, and elements can be masked by CSS selector.

setup.step: Create a free Better Stack account, then create an Errors application for your app to get an application token and ingesting host.
Install Sentry's SDK for your framework; Better Stack accepts the same SDK Sentry itself uses.
Build a DSN from the Ingest tab in the form https://APPLICATION_TOKEN@INGESTING_HOST/APPLICATION_ID and set it as the dsn wherever the SDK starts, on the server and in the browser.
Add your Telemetry API token so source maps upload on every build, using the org, project and endpoint from the application's Advanced settings tab.

builder_notes: Keep SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN (also called your Telemetry API token) out of client code and version control; it grants access to your whole Telemetry account, not just source map uploads.
The DSN itself is safe to ship to the browser, the same as with Sentry, since it only identifies where events go.
Mask HTML elements by CSS selector for session replay before recording any page that shows personal data.
